C-ADD-UI-SOUNDS.IntentSummary: Add interface sound through one SoundService behind an injectable player, wired by a route observer and a context call, with CC0 assets, a persisted hub toggle and a unit test that proves the service's three behaviours.

MustPassCommand.Command: test "$(ls assets/sfx/*.ogg | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -eq 8 && grep -qi 'CC0' assets/sfx/SOURCES.md && grep -q 'kenney.nl' assets/sfx/SOURCES.md
test -e lib/models/sfx.dart && test -e lib/services/sfx_player.dart && test -e lib/services/sound_service.dart && test -e lib/router/sound_navigator_observer.dart

T-001.Title: Declare the dependency and lay out the CC0 sound assets

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: pubspec.yaml depends on audioplayers and registers assets/sfx/ next to the existing asset folders.
Eight effects are committed: tap, navigate, back, open, close, toggle, confirm and error, each taken from the CC0 Interface Sounds pack.
assets/sfx/SOURCES.md records the pack name, the CC0 license and the kenney.nl URL, so the provenance travels with the files.
Dependencies resolve on the pinned SDK, and pubspec.lock is regenerated by that SDK rather than by whatever flutter is on PATH.

Verification.Command: test "$(ls assets/sfx/*.ogg | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -eq 8 && grep -qi CC0 assets/sfx/SOURCES.md

T-002.Title: Define the sound catalogue as an enum with an extension

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: lib/models/sfx.dart declares Sfx with the eight values and an extension mapping each to its asset path and a volume multiplier.
The file follows the repository's model style: a doc comment at the top, no codegen, the asset paths in one place.

Verification.Command: grep -q 'enum Sfx' lib/models/sfx.dart && grep -q 'extension SfxX' lib/models/sfx.dart && test "$(grep -c 'assets/sfx/' lib/models/sfx.dart)" -ge 8

T-003.Title: Put the playback behind a swappable player seam

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: lib/services/sfx_player.dart declares the interface (preload, play, dispose) and an audioplayers implementation that keeps one player per effect with ReleaseMode.stop.
Each effect's source is set once during preload, and playing reuses that source by stopping at position zero and resuming, as the package documents stop() to do.
The implementation catches platform failures so a missing audio backend degrades to silence instead of crashing the UI.
The audioplayers import appears in this file only.

T-004.Title: Add the SoundService that owns the preference, the volume and the debounce

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: SoundService extends ChangeNotifier and exposes enabled, volume, play(Sfx), preload() and setEnabled(bool).
The preference persists through SharedPreferences, following the pattern already used by the auth service.
Repeats of the same effect inside a 40 ms window are dropped, and a disabled service makes no call to the player at all.
Haptics accompany an effect on mobile, and the service never blocks a tap on I/O: play is fire-and-forget.

Verification.Command: grep -n 'class SoundService\|bool get enabled\|Future<void> play\|setEnabled\|SharedPreferences\|_minGap' lib/services/sound_service.dart | head -20

T-005.Title: Wire the service, the route observer and the app root

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AppScope registers SoundService as a ChangeNotifierProvider in dependency order, with a comment only if the order is not obvious.
lib/router/sound_navigator_observer.dart plays the navigate effect on push and the back effect on pop, and holds no other logic.
lib/app.dart passes the observer through navigatorObservers, which is currently absent, so no screen file changes for transitions.

T-006.Title: Give the hub a sound toggle that reads and writes the service

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The home hub shows an icon that reflects SoundService.enabled and flips it on tap.
Switching sound on plays the toggle effect, so the user hears what they just enabled; switching it off does not.
The icon placement does not disturb the existing hub layout at phone or desktop widths.

T-007.Title: Sound the hub tiles and the tab bar

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Pressing a hub tile and switching a tab each ask for their sound through the context call, so no screen imports the service for this.
The dead-space and scroll gestures of those widgets stay silent.

T-008.Title: Sound the dealership cards, the error retry and the daily-race surfaces

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The two dealership cards, the shared error panel's retry button and the daily-race card ask for their sound through the context call.
Opening and closing the daily-race details sheet use the open and close effects rather than a generic tap.
The refresh buttons in the daily-races screen stay silent when they are refreshed by a timer rather than by a press.

T-009.Title: Prove the service's three behaviours with a fake player

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: test/sound_service_test.dart injects a fake player and asserts that a disabled service calls it zero times, that an enabled service calls it once per play, and that a second play inside the debounce window is dropped.
The test touches no platform channel, so it runs in the normal suite without a device.

T-010.Title: Project the new module into the durable graph and verification

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: M-SOUND joins .grace/graph/main.xml and is listed in the graph index's Owns block, with its summary, path and dependencies.
V-M-SOUND joins .grace/verification/main.xml and its index, carrying the command that proves the service's behaviour and the scenarios the module must satisfy.
The scenario set records that silence is a valid outcome when sound is disabled, so a future check does not treat it as a failure.
